Large 2.5LB Professional Rock Tumbler Kit, 3-Speed Motor & 9-Day Timer, Rubber Barrel, Quiet Rotary Stone Polisher with 5 Belts, Rough Gemstones, 4 Polishing Grits, for Adults Kids (Black) My kids have recently shown interest in gems and geology, so they were super excited to try this out! This is a full kit, which means it comes with everything you need: Not only the tumbler parts, but also the various stage mixes and even the raw rocks to use!
I actually was hoping it was the sort of thing we could use more than once, learn how to use it with the included stuff and then do more of our own found rocks with the next batch! The thing is, it comes with only enough to do the included rocks, and you have to do them all at once if you want them to come out with the included materials. Beyond that, you can reuse the machine but you have to get more materials to put in with the rocks.
The machine also takes a LONG time. I knew tumbling was a process, but it's a few stages and each one takes a few days, so the whole thing took weeks of emptying out and putting in the next stage and setting the timer for the next set of days spinning. The entire process from start to finish was nearly a month. But, my kids loved it and it was a very educational experience. I wish it came with more DIY material, but I guess I'll have to find some more to do our own ones next!

text_fidelity_a:
7 Wonders We're a game playing family. With 84 board/card games and counting, I feel like something of an expert on board games. This was an exceptionally good game. Unlike some strategy games, there doesn't seem to be any one strategy that's going to always work. You have to be flexible, depending upon which wonder you end up with, the cards you get, and the strategies your opponents are using. You have to pay particular attention to the strategies of your nearest neighbors on either side because many actions and many cards play off of them. No cards or actions play directly off of an opponent who is not your neighbor. That, too, is a nice feature. It's not that you shouldn't watch what the people across the table are doing, but it's more important to know what the guys to the right and left are doing. Especially when you're dealing with higher numbers of players, that makes it easier to keep up with. That's a big part of why it works as well for 7 players as it does for 3. That, and the fact that game play is simultaneous -- no turn taking! So there's very little down time and the games moves quickly.

The only reason I didn't give this game 5 stars is that the game comes with rules for a 2-player variation that I do not believe is very good. I was hoping that this would be a game I could play with my husband after our (young) kids went to bed, but after trying several times we both agreed on two things:

1) There are much better 2-player games.
2) This game is much better with 3-7 players.

For those reasons, we will only pull it out when we have friends over. But it really, really is a top-notch game for the right number of players. I mostly wrote this review to caution people who are considering buying it more for it's two-player extendability than anything else.
text_fidelity_b: 7 Wonders

text_fidelity_a:
Magical Fairy Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Fairy House For this kit, you're paying for the convenience of having everything organized and already there. Also, for the "magical" experience you can provide for your child. If you do "Elf on a Shelf" or Santa Clause or anything similar, you'll probably love the added magical part of this kit. (We don't. We're all different and that's okay.) The parent has to be very involved. It's not a kit you just hand over to the child. (The parent portion is in a well sealed container to help keep the secret, since I imagine many parents will attempt to hand it straight over to the child. That was my plan before I realized what it was.) The child will have to do activities, and then the parent will secretly leave another activity in the fairy house. This is suppose to make the child believe the fairies left them a gift. (For example: The child is to craft 3 fairy bells and hang them around their room. Inside the fairy house, they'll place a stick, pebbles, and a leaf. They'll then spin the house and ring each bell to summon a fairy visit.)

The quality is similar to the various "Box of the Month" type subscriptions out there for kids. In my opinion, there's more in the wizard kit. There is the same amount of activities in both, but there's just not as much to do in this fairy kit. (It seems more stickers and easy crafts.) It's not high quality, but it's still nice enough. The crafts are something that could be put together with supplies from a dollar store. But, it's so convenient having everything in one place, especially for a disorganized person, like myself. Plus, there'd the "magical" experience provided for those that desire it.

Though the wizard kit that is similar to this one could work for boys and girls(and this one still could, if desired), this fairy kit is definitely targeted to girls. At the end, I couldn't help but feel sorry for all the little children doing these activities, hoping to see a fairy. While gifts are left, which are supposed to let the child know a fairy visited them, they'll never actually see one, unless the parent does something extra. We just did the crafts, since we don't do imaginary things as real. Without the added magical element, though, this kit just doesn't hold near as much value. If you're like us and don't do Santa and all, I'd recommend another kind of kit. If you do love the idea of pretending fairies are leaving gifts, this might be a blast for you and your child, as long as you don't think they'll be too disappointed that they never actually see a fairy. Overall, I found it a little disappointing, particularly considering the current price(which changes constantly).
text_fidelity_b: Magical Fairy Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Fairy House

CTSC 75FT 95FT 110FT 250FT Zipline Kit with Stainless Steel Spring Brake and Seat My kids love this. I had a couple of trees a bit over a hundred feet apart on a shallow incline, which seemed pretty perfect.

I did end up putting this together and taking it apart about ten times before I was satisfied with it, so I definitely dumped more time than I intended into it. Making adjustments is often almost as big a job as starting from scratch. The loop at the top of the line was small, and that wanted to attach to a giant redwood, so I had to switch trees, though I'm sure I could've bought a longer section of cable. The bottom end seems like it would be able to handle a big tree fine. Maybe I could've swapped ends, but it doesn't indicate that as an option anywhere. The instructions are a bit sparse, but mostly sufficient. I hadn't realized initially that the big velcro pads had a slot for the cable to go through to keep it from slipping off the pad. By the time I got everything attached high enough, I had a lot of trouble pulling all of the slack out of the line. The turnbuckle was way too short for the task. I eventually had to get creative with clamps and bungee cords to get enough mechanical advantage to pull it tight enough to clamp it down.

The included seat is nice for when you want both adults and kids to be able to use it. It allows it to be attached up high enough to be out of the way and usable by adults, while still being low enough for smaller kids to ride on the seat. My kids use it more than the trampoline, so it's a hit.

QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits This is not a “puzzle”, but a “model”. I can only assume that they do not have a word for “model” in Chinese. Because Chinese companies always list items like this is a “puzzle” though it’s really not.

This model is made of wood. It shows to have 47 pieces. There are 3 boards with the cutout pieces. You’ll want to use caution when removing the pieces from the boards so that you do not break them. You remove the pieces from the boards as you go. The pieces are numbered on the instruction sheet, but not on the boards. So if you remove them all at 1st, it will make it very difficult to put the model together. I highly recommend you have either a razor blade or thin sharp knife available to help remove the pieces. If you simply use your fingers, you could easily break a piece.

I must admit that I am not a person who likes to build models. So it took me about an hour and ½ to put this together. It turned out okay, but not as perfect as the pictures. The shingles do not fit perfectly. Nonetheless I think it looks okay.

Also, when you get to pieces 12, 13, 14 and 15 which is part of instruction number 5… Those 4 pieces make a little platform. The way the instruction show it on instruction number 9, that platform sits inside section B. But if you place it there, then the top shingle portion sits on top of the platform and is not sturdy. If you don’t put that platform there, then the top piece see fits in to the bottom piece a which makes it sturdy. Then I use that platform as a base on the bottom to place the temple on top of. Written on that platform is “Temple of Serenity”. So because of that, I think it should go on the bottom is a base anyway. But of course you can do it anyway you want to.

An optional string of LED lights is included. Two AA batteries are required and not included.

As a bonus, there is also a small “Ellie House” which is 24 pieces.

This model is made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 30 bucks I think it is a bit expensive, but it is a unique and interesting item. Also, it comes in a nice cardboard box, which makes it easy for wrapping if you’re giving it as a gift.
text_fidelity_b: QOGELY Home Decor Blaster Building Kits

What I have noticed over the years is that sometimes the simpler items are best. It is really hard to store items that are big and bulky and have a flashy plastic presentation, and even though we have a substantial area dedicated to Play-Doh, items like this which have a big piece but only perform a couple of small functions end up not being are very favorites.

This was quite fun and my children really enjoyed it. We do a lot of sprinkle cookie decorating with real cookies and sprinkles, so being able to make a thrilling series of decorated cookies was really fun for the kids, and they very much enjoyed the action of this set and getting to play with it together. They set up a fun little cookie shop making cookies and decorating them and lining up their fancy creations.

My only suggestion in future would be to make the pieces a little more modular so that they are easy for a normal family with limited space to store. I think they could easily have made the sprinkle maker hand-held and smaller, and the molds for cookies and accessories could also have been smaller and not included in a big piece of plastic.

We are an avid Hot Wheels family and always like to check out the newer sets. I love the idea of running a car around a course continuously, without relying on batteries. This set comes with a big launcher, that features a unique track with protruding tabs that catch the cars from behind as you blast them around the track. The whole idea is to catch the car(s) at the right time when it reenters the launcher, so you can have it racing around the course non-stop. Unfortunately, the course is too small and uninteresting, yet, if the layout was much larger, that launcher wouldn't have enough force without some kind of midway helper (like an automatic loop launcher). This would make a world of a difference in fun, so you you're not pounding the launcher every half second to keep the car circulating around a tiny oval which gets old fast.

Big annoyance: The launcher is very tall, so it comes in packed in two pieces which easily lock together, however, once locked, you're unable to seperate them. This is now the second set we have with this annoying problem. We like storing our hot wheels in their boxes, but once opened, there's no way to get this giant launcher back inside. Even if storing out of the box, with other toys, it's a big jalopy that could have been dismantled, taking up less space.

And finally, kids need laser-sharp hand/eye coordination to catch the car on time, so this may frustrate the impatient type. When you do manage to catch the car to keep it going, it does feel rewarding, even if it's only 2 laps. We haven't tried more than one car at a time, but I imagine on a large course, it must be fun, but on this small circuit, it's probably near impossible to work with.

LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function I really love these Duplo Lego sets. While I do not have any little ones in the house, I like having some toys on hand for the occasional visitors with kids. These are always a hit and now when friends with little ones come over, the kids always remember our place because of the "Lego Lady!" haha! Bringing out the Legos has brought shy little ones out of their shell as they put together the pieces and play away.

This train set is great! it is super simple to put together, as with any Duplo set. You will need to unscrew the battery box to put in 4 AAA batteries, though. If you're lazy like me and don't want to trudge out to the garage for a screwdriver, you can easily open it with a table knife (haha.. see pic). To make the train go, first be sure there are batteries installed and then push the on/off button on the bottom. put the train on the track. The wheels straddle the inner upright portions of the track (see pic). Then simply give the train a little push and off it goes around the track.

To control the train, use the little action tiles. These are flat pieces with a small icon on them. There is one for each of the following actions. When the train goes over it, it performs the action:
- whistle (yellow) makes a train whistle sound
- horn (white) makes one toot sound - I thought this was for the lights but those didnt come on when it went over this one
- water (blue) stops for a bit there and makes a sound like it is getting water for the steam engine
- reverse (green) stops and reverses the train
- stop (red) stops the train

The action bricks are really easy to put down on the track - they just lay in the middle of the track and don't actually attach. So it is easy for the little ones to pick them up and move them around. This is super fun for the kiddos and definitely keeps them happy occupied for quite some time!

There is an App you can get as well - works for iPhone, iPad, and Android devices. It has nothing to do with the train set itself, though. I thought maybe it did, but it is really just a separate app/Game. It is a fun little game for young kids, though. App Tip: if you have an iPhone and aren't getting any sound with the app, be sure you don't have the device on mute. (for iPhones it is that side button you switch on/off). I don't have an iPad but I suspect it could have the same issue.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function

Melissa & Doug Created by Me! Owl Pillow, 6+ years Here are some observations from my wife.

My almost-5-year-old daughter LOVES this owl pillow craft project, and so do I! She and I have just begun working on sewing with a needle and thread, but I must be sure to be with her every minute, with my hands along with hers on our first sewing projects. This pillow, however, is so smartly designed that it allows her the freedom to practice sewing buttons ON HER OWN, and she loves that freedom. I can be close to her, at the sink, putting away dishes, while she creates her pillow all by herself. It’s a big deal to her. : )

I definitely had to sit with her at the start to go through the simple instructions and to get her started on the process. She enjoyed choosing her own pattern for the owl and decided to choose the same pattern as the owl of the adorable girl on the box. I showed her how to do the first few stitches, and then she was off and running. Once she got going on her own, she kept saying, “This is so easy! This is so fun!” while working on stitching through the felt buttons.

After our first hour on the project today, she’s definitely getting the hang of the process, and she can work on it on her own with me close by for the occasional help with knotting off a thread. And though she really wanted to be able to sleep with the pillow tonight, she’s excited to spend more time stitching the felt buttons onto her owl over the coming days. I’m glad that the project will take 5-7 days of stitching for her to complete. It’s longer than just an hour or even one-day project for her, since she’s at the young side of the recommended age range (6-10 years old). It’s possible an older child could finish this project in a few hours of an afternoon.

And I have to say that I’m thrilled that it’s machine washable. Overall, this is a fantastic and adorable craft for a little one at the very beginning stages of learning to sew.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Created by Me! Owl Pillow, 6+ years

text_fidelity_a: Crayola Color Escapes Colored Pencils, 72Count, Adult Coloring, Gift I was really curious how these would compare to standard Crayola colored pencils. The difference is really only exterior. These are black with the color indicated on the bottom. The box, however, doesn’t let you see the colored bit on the bottom of the pencil, so it is really difficult to tell the color while using the box. The colors are also pretty off from the color on the bottom. Thee re hexagon shaped, so they won’t roll away from you. The actual pencil “lead” seems exactly the same as standard Crayola colored pencils. I compared them side by side and they color the same. They both have fairly soft “lead”. These are sharpened better in their presharpened state. The standard Crayola colored pencil also appear to have a bit of a chalky residue on the “lead” and these don’t, but I didn’t find that to change how they function in any way. These look a little more high end, but color pretty much the same as a Crayola colored pencil. These don’t feel like fine art quality, just hobby/craft quality. They are good for adult coloring books, which is what I got them for, so I’m happy with them. They just aren’t the quality of higher end colored pencils as they are packaged to have you believe.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Color Escapes Colored Pencils, 72Count, Adult Coloring, Gift

All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions [[VIDEOID:moOM6Q7TMDWRNW]]This is like an awesome mix between Apples to Apples and Trivial Pursuit. It's played very similarly to Apples to Apples, but you have an open-ended question, and everyone writes answers down on a piece of paper. Then the pieces of paper are handed in, and the person who is It has to guess who wrote what question. The person who is It gets one point per right answer that they match with the people playing the game.

It's a fun, and simple concept, which makes for a fun and simple game. And, the questions are awesome. I've gotten a few "getting to know you" books in the past, which have lists of supposedly interesting questions. All of those books pale in comparison to this awesome game. These questions are intense, interesting, and none of them put too much pressure on you.

My girlfriend and I found ourselves just reading the questions and answering them a lot, just by ourselves. It's a great way to talk about tons of different topics than the ones that usually come up. Like I said, these questions are great.

I usually really don't like party games like this. I usually like strategy games better. But this is one party game that I love.

Pros:
+Awesome questions
+Fun game
+Good quality
+Well designed

Cons:
-You need 4 people to play according to the rules, even though these are fun questions to ask if there are just two or three of you
text_fidelity_b: All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions

Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up I have been enjoying this as a solo game but am happy that it won't be hard to teach friends.

Unlike some games there isn't a finite number of turns...the game ends when someone defeats the boss then each players points are tallied. I like that aspect a lot.

There are some "power" type blocks that benefit all players when one player has success with it.

The art is very cool and whimsical. The paper is sufficient but not very heavy duty. You get plenty of maps...there are 4 of each distinct map design. It's a busy map and I plan on taking the cheapest route possible and using regular sheet protectors and dry erase markers.

I'm not liking the wooden dice at all. For the money I would have really liked some fancier dice. Maybe bigger...maybe more colorful.
You get 4 short presharpened pencils that ...don't have erasers and your first game or two you might need to correct something.

Basically this could have been a print and play. There's nothing at all spectacular about the contents.

My personal little gripe is I don't see how you can be in two places at once. You can attack the map from different sides of the map moving in from starter sections.

That's seems like a lot of negativity but it is a fun little game anyway. You can play it on a small table or most places since there aren't components other than a map and the dice. Also this can encourage people to play who maybe aren't that into games since you don't unload tons of intimidating cards, counters and pieces.

It's a very fine experience. It could've been better for the money though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up

Marbotic - Sensory Kit for iPad - Wooden Interactive Lowercase Letters and Numbers for Learning to Read & Maths -Ages from 2 to 5- Used in Kindergartens I generally don't prefer electronic learning, but these are pretty cool. The Smart Letters each have three rubber feet that are spaced differently, and the tablet recognizes the letter when you gently place it on the tablet screen. It took about 10 minutes to download all 6 free apps (3 for letters, 3 for numbers) and to set up the quick profile. The apps are simple to use and well designed. Next is a summary of the 3 letter apps:

Bla Bla Box: spell out words and hear them read back to you
Alphamonster: choose a letter to hear the sound the letter makes and see a picture of a word beginning with that letter. See a picture of an item and identify what letter the item starts with. Hear a sound of a letter and identify the letter. See a cursive lowercase letter and identity the matching wooden uppercase letter. (In the settings you can pick which letters will appear throughout these challenges. The default is the entire alphabet but you can pick just a few if your child needs to focus on certain letters)
Vocabubble: game 1- pick any letter and as you repeatedly place the letter on the tablet, 8 different pictures of items beginning with that letter will fall down the screen. Game 2 - choose two letters, then pictures of items beginning with those two letters will fall down the screen and you tap the picture with the right letter in order for it to disappear. (This was a fun game my niece and nephew enjoyed playing together as they each held a letter. However, some pictures seemed too hard or random for a 5 year old, such as an Orca for the letter O... kids will think it's a Whale... or a Totem Pole or Quaill, etc)

My five year old niece and nephew enjoyed testing these for me and were definitely interested in the games. I'm excited to start my daughter with it when she turns three and I can see the number apps extending the usefulness of the product as she gets older. Four stars, not five, only because they do seem a bit pricey and also because the accent on the American English setting we tried out is a bit odd at times.
text_fidelity_b: Marbotic - Sensory Kit for iPad - Wooden Interactive Lowercase Letters and Numbers for Learning to Read & Maths -Ages from 2 to 5- Used in Kindergartens

text_fidelity_a:
WireJewelry Double Barrel Rock Tumbler with (2) 3 Pound Capacity Drums My boys young boys have been rockhounds ever since we moved to Eastern Oregon three years ago. We thought we'd add the the thrill and enjoyment by getting them a tumbler to further explore the joys of rock hunting. There's a certain thrill of putting in raw stones that you think are "pretty", only to see their true beauty one they are polished.

We already have a single barrel WireJewelry tumbler and love it so much that we decided to grab this one to expand our capability. (There are LOTS of rocks here).

As before, assembly and setup was easy. Allowing one to have six total pounds of capacity is amazing. The heavy duty motor doesn't seem to be strained at all, even under full load, so it should last years. The barrel construction is very sturdy and we have never had even a minor leak. By design, they are very well sealed. While the noise level is not bad, I find it best to do my rock tumbling in the garage. The same hum in your house for weeks on end might just get to you.

This company is great for packaging kits, not only for the tumbling media, but for rocks as well. The media kids come numbered and labeled, so the process is super easy to follow. Tumbling is not a quick hobby... each batch can take weeks. Personally, I think that's part of the fun.

If you are thinking of getting into the hobby, I definitely recommend products from WireJewelry, I have yet to be disappointed in their products. Enjoy the treasure hunt!
text_fidelity_b: WireJewelry Double Barrel Rock Tumbler with (2) 3 Pound Capacity Drums

Nerf N-Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster I chuckled when I read the "how would you rate this toy's educational value" question above, because let me tell you, I've been schoolin' everyone in the house with this thing. Don't eat my cookies. Blam! Don't make fun of my shoes. Blam! I'm a girl, you don't get to snicker about my lip balm collection. Blam!

If you're within 20 feet of someone, you're pretty well guaranteed to bean them on the behind with this thing. And it stings! Not enough to bruise, but enough so they don't want to get beaned again soon.

It's also entertaining for the cats. My adventurous boy kitty loves to chase things, so I aim the dart gun down the hallway and he has a blast sprinting after the darts when they bounce off the wall. He also has a blast chewing the darts into unfortunate shapes after, but for the most part they're still usable. I bought some spare ones for a few bucks more.

While I initially got this thinking of my seven-year-old niece, it was obvious upon arrival that she was not nearly tough enough for this thing. For one, I pinched the side of my finger while messing with it - not fun - and then I just generally found I needed to use some muscle to assemble and disassemble it. Plus, I didn't think she was quite old enough to get the whole "for reals, yo, don't shoot people in the face" deal. I'd say the age guideline is just about right, I don't think I'd give this to anyone under eight, if only for my own sanity.

Overall, this is a pretty kickin' toy and one I'm glad I ordered. Be prepared to buy more darts if you take it outside, though.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf N-Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster

text_fidelity_a:
Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome My almost four year-old boy loves the Fisher-Price Power Wheels Dune Racer Chrome Ride-On. This means it passed the most important reviewing test. Overall, I also like it, but some things could be improved.

Pro
* It looks cool with its sky blue and chrome features, with black seats and slick black wheels. He's the first kid in preschool with a rad set of wheels.
* It goes forward 2.5 and 5.0 mph, and backward 2.5 mph.
* Steering is actual. The driver could parallel park if needed.
* It auto breaks when the pedal is let go. Nice safety feature.

Con
* Chrome and other parts scratch easily, and even arrived scratched a little
* It took over 90 minutes to put together, and some parts had to muscled in.
* Not everything lines up easily. This isn't just aesthetic, but includes the front wheels. We are still trying to get them properly aligned.
* Seat doesn't move. My boy can barely reach the pedals despite being almost four (the stated age is 4-7). Moving forward, we'll include a back cushion.
* While it too early to be sure, the tires (hollow hard plastic) look like they'll wear quickly.
* I weigh too much. I want to ride in it!

Lots of fun, and a great way to bring your child along on long walks.

Anthony Trendl
treefortbooks.com
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome

Harrisville Designs Lap Loom Kit, Hand Weaving for Kids and Adults (Style B) I used to make wall hangings as a child with homemade looms. I recently met someone who weaves huge items and after seeing photos of her work my interest in weaving was renewed. I like the simplicity of these looms but do have some comments. Firstly, the frame is wood with plastic pegs. A screw in each corner holds the frame together but mine is a bit loose. I may need to tighten later. Instruction booklet is well written, read all the way through before starting because there are tips later on in the booklet. Parents please note that every other row you must insert a second flat shed stick into the loom. It's not complicated, just takes time so be aware if your child may not have patience to do this.
My only complaint is I ordered the bigger size B loom and in the photo on Amazon it showed yarn in orange, yellow and reds so I bought a refill yarn kit called Sierra because it was black and red and I thought it would be nice to have both but when my loom arrived I see the size B comes with the black and red yarn and the smaller sized A has the oranges. So now I'll have two black and red items :( I don't know where the photo came from but it should be corrected!
The manufacturers website shows the correct colors but I didn't go there until after I got my loom. I would also recommend spending $10 more to get the Wonderloom. It helps push the yarn down evenly.
This loom is a good size for making place mats.

SmartLab Toys It's Alive Slime Lab SmartLab Toys It’s Alive Slime Lab is just one of dozens and dozens of slime toys intended to fascinate the young scientist in your home. The way most of these labs works is similar: Combine the included slime mix, if any exists, with a few household items like baking soda, vinegar, cornstarch, etc., and let the fun begin.

This slime toy works like the others in terms of the mixing, but it is also different than others, and I mean that in a good way. With this slime lab, the mixture is placed atop a motor that vibrates for greater effect. Kids can watch the colors and textures swirl around as the vibrations create some fun and very visual patterns. The instructions include 20 different recipes for slime and each can be made using items found in most kitchens.

What I probably like best about this slime lab is the lack of mess! Okay, there is some mess but in relative terms, the messiness is kept under control very well. The key difference is that, with most other slime labs my kids have used, messiness is encouraged. These other labs involve sticking hands in the slime, spreading it with your hands, and so on. This is messy and gross, and if multiple kids are involved, they often end up smearing it on each other, splattering it on the floors and more. There is no problem like that with SmartLab. The slime, for the most part, stays in the bowl, out of your way.

Educational toys are nice and SmartLab Toys It’s Alive Slime Lab is a toy that does get kids thinking and asking questions. My girls like it and have returned to it more than once, creating more slime and learning about household chemicals and how they react. It’s a good choice of toy that will keep kids entertained as they learn.
text_fidelity_b: SmartLab Toys It's Alive Slime Lab

LEGO City Race Boat Transporter 60254 Race Boat Toy, Fun Building Set for Kids (238 Pieces) This LEGO CITY RACE BOAT TRANSPORTER BUILDING SET ((60254) New 2020, 238 Pieces) is fairly easy to build--the difficulty is what I’d call “normal” for a City-themed set. City sets are among my favorites, because they include fire trucks, police stations, buses, trains, beachgoer minifigs, space stations, and all the rest of the things that a bustling city (or the airspace above it) needs. This particular set is aimed at ages 5 and up.

The set contains all the pieces required to build three separate items: a semi-trailer truck (for towing the race boat), a trailer for hauling the race boat, and a race boat. (You can use the truck’s trailer hitch to tow other things that you build, of course.)

The “Xtreme” graphics are NOT printed on the pieces, but are applied with stickers. (I hate stickers, too.) Applying stickers is made easier if you first stick a corner to something long and thin (e.g., a spudger or a plastic knife) so that you can better control the placement on the element. A good thing about LEGO stickers is that they can be removed and replaced (like Post-Its) if you get them misaligned.

The LEGO elements are compatible with other City sets and with all regular LEGO sets (but not with DUPLO sets, which have extra-large pieces for very young builders). The Race Boat Transporter set is another fine addition to the extensive collection of City sets.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO City Race Boat Transporter 60254 Race Boat Toy, Fun Building Set for Kids (238 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure (Due to the malfunctions on our particular dog, and the fact that he doesn't walk at all, I was tempted to give it 3 stars, but he's so cute and fun, I went with 4.)

I have a few Paw Patrol fans in my house, so this is a pretty amazing toy.

By pressing the badge on the front of Chase, your children are given a mission. Chase talks and interacts through these missions. For example, chickens have gotten loose, and your child needs to help gather them up. The net compartment opens up, and your child will fire the net out. Chase comments on catching one, and then asks for the net to be reloaded. (One time the net got stuck, and didn't fire out, but he still exclaimed praise at catching a chicken, so it's not perfect.) He won't interact to various things that your child says, but he does have built in interaction, which is still pretty cool.

There are 24 different missions, and Chase moves around a bit through these. I was expecting him to walk a bit, but he never did. He just moves his head around, and moves from crouching to standing positions. There are two compartments on his backpack. One has a net launcher. The other has a microphone(that your child can talk into) and a flashlight. There are various buttons for each feature. (One for opening each compartment, one on the net launcher to launch, one to make the light come on the flashlight, and one to turn on the microphone.) Some of the items come on automatically through missions, but others require your child's assistance, when Chase asks.

Although this is an awesome toy that I'm pretty sure any Paw Patrol fan will love, we did have a couple of negatives with ours.

When the box was first opened, the head was detached a bit, but thankfully, it went back on pretty easily. Also, the button to launch the microphone/flashlight wouldn't work. I tried everything I could to make it work, short of tearing it apart, and tried numerous times, but it never worked. It didn't work when it was supposed to automatically open during missions, either. Thankfully, we can just pull that compartment open. During missions when a child is asked to launch the microphone/flashlight, pulling open the door makes the task recognized, just as if the button worked. So, it's not a huge deal, but still disappointing.

I really do wish he walked a bit, too! The way he's designed, it looked as if he would.

A couple of notes:
-This toy DOES come with batteries, but require 4 AA if you'd like to buy extras.
-If your child can read, know that the box this is delivered in says what's inside, though there are no pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure

Lost Cities - The Board Game Lost Cities TBG is a lot like the original Lost Cities Card Game, but it supports more than 2-players. That's a nice feature.

For those who don't know, Lost Cities the Card Game is considered legendary among hobby board gamers because it's simple, but deep, meaning that anyone can pick up the rules to the game quite quickly, but there's interesting decision-making and complex outcomes to worry about based on your decisions. Of course, it's only a 2-player game, which can be a downfall for many.

The Board Game version is similar in terms of gameplay. If you've already experienced the card game, I could teach you this version in about 30 seconds. Unfortunately, you'll soon want to be back playing the card game. This game lacks a certain something to make it really fun. It works, and it's still easy to learn and play, but I don't think I'll come back to it all that often unless I'm playing with my daughter. For those who are into more complex games, this one just feels...old fashioned. In all the ways that the card game has aged well, this one hasn't.

text_fidelity_a: Manhattan Toy Whoozit Activity Spiral Stroller and Travel Activity Toy I bought this toy thinking it would be good to use on my doorway jumperoo.  The jumperoo has two rings on the two front suspension straps to hang toys on.  But when I got the Whoozit Activity Spiral, it turns out it is very tightly coiled, like a spring; not flexible or bendable.  It is difficult to uncoil it or to stretch it out.  And there is no mechanism to attach it to things.  Although it seems to advertise that you can wrap it around anything, this is completely not true.  There is no wire or anything inside it to attach it with.  If you feed it through a hole, it might stay.  But in the case of my jumperoo, it wouldn't stay hooked on, but just coiled back up and fell off.  So then I tried it on the baby's carseat.  Again, it wouldnt' stay on.  It was too short to wrap a coil from each end around the bars of the car seat, so it would just slide up to the top of the bar as it contracted, or it would fall right off.  IF it were made of something stretchier, or if it had wire inside that would allow you to wrap the ends around something, it might be good. I think the baby would like the little dangling toys on it.  But as it is, it won't attach to anything we have.  And when it is so tightly coiled (as it is all the time unless you're stretching it out yourself) the toys are all jumbled up in the coils and not visible or reachable for baby.  So to me it is a pretty useless toy.

The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up Several years ago there was a British series about Robin Hood, and my family and I have been hooked ever since seeing that series. This game seemed like a good fit for my family based on our interests, and so far it has been a good addition to family game night. That said, this game tends to be on the easy side and the replayability isn't great if you want a varying experience.

In a nutshell, this is a basic move-around-the-board game at its heart, though it requires cooperation instead of competition and it relies on a story book to further the game along. Some real time and attention to detail went into the design and it shows.

Though the game does not require following a path without turning to the left or right, it does follow a basic flow and the story book is designed to help guide and direct. That said, it essentially is a map of how to get through each step and it does not vary from game to game so once the game has been played the book could potentially slow down a game instead of moving it along at an interesting pace since previous players will know what to do.

This is certainly not a bad game. It's a good family game and is worth running through as a group. However, for those looking for replayability, this one lacks variety.
text_fidelity_b: The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up
